content.text: targeting the anagen hair follicles (scalp MC)
that develop over a period of weeks (painless & not pruritic)
: short hairs broken off a few mm
from scalp w/ tapering near the proximal hair shaft
(exclamation point appearance) at the margins of the patches
no erythema, inflammation, or scarring seen
(definitive): peribulbar lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrates surrounding the follicles
; may be observed in mild cases
Genetically predetermined progressive loss of the terminal hairs on the scalp in a characteristic distribution (pattern)
▪︎MC type of hair loss in men & women
▪︎gradual in onset & usually occurs after puberty
; activation of androgen receptor shortens anagen (growth phase) in normal hair growth cycle, pathologic specimens show decreased anagen to telogen ratio
: begins as bitemporal thinning of the frontal scalp then involves the vertex
: thinning of the hair between the frontal & vertex of the scalp w/o affecting the frontal hairline
: widens blood vessels, allowing more blood,
oxygen, & nutrients to promote the anagen phase
: Scopulariopsis brevicaulis, Aspergillus spp., Hendersonula toruloidea
: DM, immunodeficiency (HIV⊕), poor circulation, PAD, tinea pedis (including close contacts)
: clinical + confirmation of fungal infection (culture + KOH/PAS)
Infection of the lateral & proximal nail folds <6wks
: occurs after penetrating skin trauma (biting nails, dishwashing, cuticle damage during manicures, ingrown nails)
Painful, red, swollen area around the proximal or lateral nail folds at the cuticle
